findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Commit candidate 3's Titan embedding vectors (keyed like digests.json) so the vector recall table is recomputable offline, or scope AC2's re-run/reproducibility requirement to exclude the un-entitled live Titan path explicitly.
evidence: 'The returned TicketDigest JSON is committed to evals/similar-tickets/digests.json ... so the recall tables are recomputable from the committed fixture with no model access' — scoped to candidate 2 only
'Checked by re-running each command and matching the ADR tables' (AC2) applies to all three candidates
'run candidate 3 under a developer AWS identity holding Titan entitlement (a one-off offline eval)' — not reproducible without that identity
ABSENCE: no committed embeddings/vectors file for candidate 3 analogous to digests.json
findings.finding: Acceptance criterion 2 requires candidate 3's recall@5/@10 be reproducible by 're-running each command and matching the ADR tables', and the plan states the recall tables are 'recomputable from the committed fixture with no model access' — but only candidate 2's digests are committed to digests.json; candidate 3's Titan embeddings are never committed. Because candidate 3 needs live Titan entitlement that is explicitly NOT present today and is run under a one-off developer identity, its recall table cannot be re-verified offline or by any non-entitled reviewer, defeating the reproducibility the AC asserts.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 2; Approach candidate 3; Scope (digests.json committed, no embeddings file)
findings.suggested_fix: Add evals/similar-tickets/embeddings.json keyed by ticket id + SHA-256 of the embedded text + model id, committed alongside digests.json, so brute-force cosine recall for candidate 3 is reproducible with no Bedrock access.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that candidate 3 produces real per-stratum recall@5/@10 against live Titan (under the entitled developer identity recorded in the fixture header), OR explicitly state that an ADR finalized with candidate 3 'unavailable' is an invalid terminal state and the story is not done until the vector path has been measured.

findings.finding: The vector candidate (candidate 3, live Titan embedding) is the novel path the epic's decision hinges on, yet no acceptance criterion requires it to actually run live and produce real recall numbers — the plan explicitly lets it record 'unavailable' on AccessDeniedException, and the ADR may be completed (AC3) while excluding an unavailable candidate. The whole architecture decision could thus be finalized without the vector path ever executing.
findings.location: Approach candidate 3 / Auth precondition / AC2 / AC3 / Testing
scenarios: Executor runs in an environment without Titan entitlement, records candidate 3 unavailable, and writes an ADR choosing between only lexical and digest candidates — leaving the epic's vector-vs-not question unmeasured.
findings.suggested_fix: Make 'measure.py --candidate vector' producing committed recall numbers a required AC, gated on the recorded entitlement check in the fixture header, so completion requires the vector path to have actually executed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile candidate 3's embedding input description so both the Approach bullet and the Digest-serialization paragraph state the same construction (field-name-prefixed one-line-per-field, 40,000-char truncation).

Digest serialization: 'Candidate 3 embeds the same four in the same order as one paragraph, each on one line prefixed by its field name, truncated to 40,000 characters'

scenarios: Executor reads candidate 3 line and emits a free-paragraph join; a reviewer reads the serialization paragraph and expects field-name-prefixed lines.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the per-ticket fallback for the digest sub-step (candidates 2 and 3): what measure.py does when a single ticket's trivial-model digest call errors or returns a payload that fails TicketDigest validation — abort, retry, or skip-with-record — distinct from the candidate-level AccessDenied/credentials-absent skip.
evidence: Plan specifies only the candidate-wide skip: 'The credentials-absent skip is widened to catch AccessDeniedException, recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting'.

Plan commits the returned TicketDigest JSON to digests.json 'keyed by ticket id plus a SHA-256 of digest_input and the prompt text; the runner reuses a cached digest on a key match and calls the model only on a miss' — but says nothing about a miss whose call fails or whose response fails TicketDigest validation.

TicketDigest is a structured-output contract (per the plan and ADR 0086:39), so a model response can validate-fail independently of credentials/entitlement — a distinct failure mode from the AccessDenied path the plan does cover.
findings.finding: The plan specifies a candidate-level fallback (AccessDeniedException or absent Bedrock credentials -> candidate 3 recorded `unavailable`) but never specifies the per-ticket fallback for the digest LLM sub-step: what measure.py does when a single ticket's `trivial`-model digest call errors (timeout/transient) or returns a payload that fails TicketDigest structured-output validation. This feeds both candidate 2 (BM25F over digests) and candidate 3 (embeds of the digest), so an unspecified single-ticket failure is ambiguous between abort, skip-the-ticket (dropping it from the index and silently biasing recall), or retry.
findings.location: Approach, candidate 2 (digest lexical) and the 'Auth precondition' paragraph
scenarios: A single ticket's digest call times out or the trivial model returns malformed/partial JSON that fails TicketDigest validation during fixture build.
A ticket whose digest is absent from digests.json on a cache miss while running without model access.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify retry/backoff (or resumable caching) for transient Bedrock errors on the per-ticket digest and embedding calls, distinct from the permanent AccessDeniedException handling.
evidence: 'One call per ticket, fed exactly the fixture's digest_input'

'The credentials-absent skip is widened to catch AccessDeniedException, recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting' — covers permanent auth failure only, not transient throttles
ABSENCE: no retry/backoff mentioned for transient Bedrock errors across the per-ticket model-call loops
findings.finding: The plan adds external Bedrock model calls (Claude Haiku for digests, Titan for embeddings) but specifies error handling only for the credentials-absent and AccessDeniedException cases (mark candidate unavailable). A transient Bedrock throttle (429 / ThrottlingException) mid-run during the one-call-per-ticket digest loop or the embedding loop has no retry/backoff and no stated handling, so a single transient failure would either abort the run or silently corrupt the recall table.
findings.suggested_fix: Since digests are already cached per key, state that a transient Bedrock error is retried with backoff and that the cache is written incrementally per ticket so a re-run resumes from the last committed entry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition per Bedrock failure arm: AccessDeniedException/credentials-absent = permanent (candidate 'unavailable', never selected); throttle/timeout = transient/retryable (retried, not marked unavailable).
evidence: 'recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting — and an unavailable candidate may not be selected by the ADR'
ABSENCE: no explicit disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) distinguishing a 429 throttle from an AccessDeniedException
findings.finding: The plan alters the Bedrock failure path (widening the skip to catch AccessDeniedException) but states dispositions only informally. It does not label dispositions with explicit words: AccessDeniedException/credentials-absent is effectively permanent/fatal-for-this-run (candidate marked unavailable, may not be selected), while a Bedrock throttle is retryable/transient — the plan never distinguishes them, so a retryable throttle could be misclassified as the same 'unavailable' terminal state as a permanent auth denial.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State plainly that candidate 1 uses FTS5's column-weighted bm25() (not field-aware BM25F) and candidate 2 uses the bespoke BM25F scorer, so the ADR records each candidate's actual ranking function accurately.
evidence: Plan: candidate 1 'SQLite FTS5 with bm25() over title (weight 5.0) and description (weight 1.0)'; candidate 2 'BM25F over LLM digests' indexing 'four as BM25F fields'.

sqlite.org/fts5.html (retrieved): bm25() applies per-column weights into one BM25 calculation with a row-level length — secondary sources (ingoampt.com, retrieved) state explicitly 'FTS5 column weighting is not full BM25F. BM25F performs more elaborate field-aware normalisation.'
ADR 0086 itself distinguishes 'Field-weighted BM25F ... a bespoke ~40-LOC scorer' from FTS5.
findings.finding: The plan labels candidate 1 as 'SQLite FTS5 with bm25()' while candidate 2 is 'BM25F' with a bespoke scorer, but FTS5's bm25() is column-weighted BM25, not true field-aware BM25F — an unresolved capability/terminology conflation that will misdescribe the recorded method in the ADR.
findings.location: Approach — candidate 1 (Lexical baseline) and candidate 2 (Digest lexical)
scenarios: The ADR records candidate 1 as BM25/BM25F; a reader reproducing results via FTS5 cannot tell whether field-aware normalization was expected, and candidate-2 weights (propositions 3.0 etc.) imply a true BM25F the FTS5 path cannot deliver.
findings.suggested_fix: Call candidate 1 'FTS5 column-weighted BM25' and reserve 'BM25F' for candidate 2's bespoke field-aware scorer (as ADR 0086 did), noting the normalization difference.

findings.finding: The plan reintroduces a vector/embedding retrieval candidate (candidate 3, Titan) without citing ADR 0086 — the directly preceding design record for this same problem/epic — which ran a measured experiment and explicitly chose 'Cupid digests WITHOUT embeddings' (arXiv:2308.10022), rejecting embeddings and ANN on measured grounds.
findings.location: Approach — candidate 3 (Vector); and the ADR deliverable
